question_it_answers: Are people using the assistant at all?
how_to_compute: Agents with 1+ assistant session in the week / agents on shift that week
evidence_needed: Descriptive (trend since launch; no comparison group needed)
notes: Adoption, not impact. In the A01 synthetic data it reaches about 0.80 once established, yet it says nothing about how many more tickets got resolved

question_it_answers: Is the use real or just logging in?
how_to_compute: Sessions where a suggestion was accepted or a draft sent / all sessions
notes: Guards against counting curiosity clicks as adoption

metric: Share of tickets answered with an assistant draft
question_it_answers: Has the way work gets done changed?
how_to_compute: Tickets whose first reply started from an assistant draft / tickets handled
evidence_needed: Descriptive vs. the team's own pre-launch baseline
notes: Behavior change is a mechanism; it still is not impact

question_it_answers: Are assisted replies as accurate and compliant as unassisted ones?
how_to_compute: QA-sampled assisted replies passing policy and accuracy checks / assisted replies sampled (sample at least 50 per team-month)
example_target: at or above the unassisted rate
red_flag: more than 3 pp below the unassisted rate
evidence_needed: Descriptive (assisted vs. unassisted replies in the same weeks)
notes: Blind the QA reviewers to whether a reply was assisted. Agents choose which tickets to draft with the assistant, so assisted vs. unassisted is not a fair comparison on its own; compare against the team's pre-launch QA rate as well

question_it_answers: Did productivity rise because of the assistant?
how_to_compute: Tickets resolved / logged agent-hours per team-week; estimate the effect with DiD against teams not yet launched (staggered estimator if launches are spread out)
evidence_needed: Comparison group required: DiD with not-yet-launched teams; check parallel pre-trends; never before-after alone
notes: In A01 the before-after gain is +0.60, the DiD effect +0.30: half the apparent gain would have happened anyway

question_it_answers: Did speed come at the cost of quality?
how_to_compute: Resolved tickets reopened within 7 days / tickets resolved; same DiD design as the speed metric
example_target: DiD effect: 95% CI upper bound below +1.0 pp
evidence_needed: Comparison group required (same design as the paired speed metric)
notes: Report next to every speed number. In A01 the reopen-rate DiD is +0.09 pp (95% CI -0.22 to +0.40 pp): quality held

metric: Fully loaded cost per resolved ticket
question_it_answers: Is the operation cheaper per unit of work?
how_to_compute: (Agent cost + assistant licence and run cost) / tickets resolved; translate the rung-3 causal effect, not the before-after change
evidence_needed: Comparison group (rung-3 causal estimate) x finance assumptions; state the assumptions
notes: Use the DiD effect (+0.30) for the business case. The naive +0.60 would double the claimed savings

metric: Customer satisfaction (CSAT) or customer effort score
question_it_answers: Do customers experience the same or better service?
how_to_compute: Survey CSAT on resolved tickets; same DiD design (or matched survey windows) as rung 3
example_target: no drop vs. comparison (95% CI lower bound above -2 points)
evidence_needed: Comparison group required; watch survey response-rate changes
notes: Savings that cost customers are not value
